record.title: Bonfim traders’ interrupted freight blockade over access to Lethem, September 2021
record.scope: Brazilian approach and fiscal-post gate near the Takutu/Tacutu bridge; obstruction of supply trucks bound for Lethem
record.direction: Brazil to Guyana freight movement obstructed.
record.movement: Goods trucks travelling from Brazil to Lethem, including essential supplies.
record.exceptions: Goods could reach Lethem by alternative routes. No claim that all border movement stopped.
record.imposing_authority: Bonfim residents, traders, taxi drivers and truckers
record.enforcement: Protesters blocked the highway approach and fiscal-post gate.
record.consequences: Delayed supplies; alternative deliveries mitigated reported shortages.
record.relationship: Promotes R4-AM-L004. Distinct non-state obstruction of permitted freight during the national COVID regime R4-AM-003; not a second count of that entry policy.
record.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
record.official_rationale: Protesters demanded reciprocal access to work and trade in Lethem, alleging unequal treatment under pandemic travel restrictions.
record.context: Guyana’s underlying travel regime allowed weekly goods deliveries. Protesters obstructed that permitted trade; talks on personal travel subsequently eased the dispute.
record.uncertainty: The initial action stopped and restarted on September 15. News Room reported goods arriving again before September 29, while Stabroek confirmed the protest ended by October 2. The precise final removal date and permitted movements during the resumed blockade remain unresolved.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. First action September 9; stopped and restarted September 15. Protest reported ended by October 2; exact final endpoint left null. No continuous interval.

Initial action ended then resumed; no continuous spell or final day inferred.
